title: Axeyum Carrier Correspondence Ledger
description: The carrier correspondence ledger: one JSON file, `artifacts/carrier-correspondence/carrier-correspondence-v1.json`, with one `rows[]` entry per (Axeyum carrier, Mathlib counterpart) pair -- the object-level sibling of theorem-correspondence.schema.json (which adjudicates two FACTS as the same idea; this adjudicates two CARRIERS -- types, or typeclass/record spines -- as the same, stronger, weaker, different, or absent). It exists because `docs/math-department/14-lean-lang.md` Next Ten item 4 found that reviewers 03, 05, 07 and 08 each have a carrier this repository shares no written mapping for, so a sentence like 'we proved the theorem Mathlib has' could not be checked -- only asserted. Each row names both carriers with a verified source location, the equality regime on each side (this kernel is built from setoids and defined `Equiv`/`Apart` relations where Mathlib is a classical Cauchy or Quot.sound quotient -- ADR-0512, ADR-1588), a grade from a closed enum, a one-sentence reason, and -- for every grade except `no-counterpart` -- at least one concrete theorem pair as the witness the grade rests on. `scripts/check-carrier-correspondence.py --check` enforces the closed enum, resolves every Axeyum name against the live kernel projection (`artifacts/autogenesis/kernel-dependency-projection-v1.json`), and requires the witness. A name that could not be verified is recorded with `verification: "unverified"` rather than silently guessed.

id.description: `CC:` for carrier-correspondence, distinct from `F:` facts, `X:` theorem-correspondences, `C:`/`K:`/`L:` overlay entities -- an id says what kind of thing it names. Must be unique across `rows[]`; enforced by the checker, not by this schema.

title.description: One line naming both carriers, e.g. "CReal, a Bishop-style regular-sequence real, against Mathlib's Cauchy-quotient Real".

carrier.description: The Axeyum-side name, e.g. `CReal`, `Nat.Finset`, `AlgS.Group`, `Nat.RM`. Need not itself be a single kernel declaration id -- it may be the family/module the row is about, or may explain that the brief's named object does not exist -- but every `witness[].axeyum_theorem` must resolve exactly.

source_location.description: `file:line` inside this repository where the carrier is defined or first declared. `null` only when `verification` is `unverified`.

verification.description: `verified-in-kernel-projection`: the carrier (or its representative declaration) is an `id` in `artifacts/autogenesis/kernel-dependency-projection-v1.json`. `verified-in-source-only`: confirmed present in `crates/axeyum-lean-kernel/src` but the projection does not carry a matching id (e.g. a module-level family name rather than one declaration, or a declaration that postdates the projection's last regeneration). `unverified`: could not be confirmed either way -- named honestly rather than guessed, per the brief's discipline.

verification_detail.description: What was actually run to verify -- a grep/shape_search command or projection lookup, or the reason verification could not complete.

equality_regime.description: `eq`: kernel-primitive `Eq`. `setoid`: a defined `Equiv`/`Apart`-style relation distinct from `Eq` (ADR-0512/ADR-1588). `quotient`: a genuine `Quot`-built type (this kernel has none by construction -- `Quot.sound` is a registered absence, ADR-0780). `none`: not a carrier with an equality of its own (e.g. a derivability relation or a logic-fragment family). `other`: something not covered, explained in the note.

equality_regime_note.description: The specific relation and how it differs from bare `Eq`, e.g. "CReal.Equiv: a defined Prop-valued closeness relation over regular rational sequences, not literal Eq".

counterpart.description: The Mathlib name, e.g. `Real`, `Finset`, `Group`, `SimpleGraph`. `null` only when `grade` is `no-counterpart`.

module_path.description: The Mathlib module the counterpart is declared in, e.g. `Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic`. `null` only when `counterpart` is `null`.

source_location.description: `file:line` (or `file:line-line`) inside the pinned mathlib4 checkout (commit `c5ea00351c28e24afc9f0f84379aa41082b1188f`, Lean 4.30.0). `null` only when `counterpart` is `null`.

verification.description: `verified-in-pinned-checkout`: read directly from the pinned mathlib4 checkout (`scripts/provision-lean-import-toolchain.sh --verify` names its path), never from memory. `unverified`: a plausible name that could not be confirmed against the checkout on this host. `not-applicable`: `grade` is `no-counterpart` and there is nothing to verify.

verification_detail.description: The grep/read that confirmed (or failed to confirm) the counterpart and its file:line, or why none was searched (no-counterpart rows should still record the negative search, e.g. "grep -ri 'rado' across Mathlib/ : 0 matches, positive control 'AffineSubspace' 53 as a sanity check that the tree is readable").

equality_regime.description: `eq`: an ordinary structure/typeclass whose intended equality is literal `Eq`. `quotient-eq`: a `Quot`-built type where distinct representatives become propositionally `Eq` via `Quot.sound` (e.g. `Real`, `Multiset`). `classical-prop`: a bare `Prop`-valued relation with no witness/data content. `none`/`other` as on the Axeyum side.

equality_regime_note.description: As `axeyum.equality_regime_note`, or a short reason when `equality_regime` is `none` (no-counterpart rows).

grade.description: `same-statement`: stripping the carrier from both formal statements leaves the identical proposition (the theorem-correspondence schema's `carrier-transport` shape, applied to the carrier pair as a whole). `constructively-stronger`: the Axeyum side proves a strictly stronger or more computational statement over the same content (a witness/algorithm where Mathlib has a bare existence or classical instance) -- ADR-1030's IVT verdict is the worked example. `constructively-weaker`: the reverse -- Mathlib's classical route reaches further than this kernel's constructive one on the same content. `different-object`: the two are not comparable on one axis -- either the hypotheses and conclusions differ in the same direction (ADR-1030's EVT verdict) or the carriers serve genuinely different purposes despite a superficial name match. `no-counterpart`: nothing in the pinned Mathlib checkout plays this role at all.

reason.description: One sentence giving the specific reason for the grade -- not a restatement of the grade's definition.

witness.description: Concrete theorem pairs the grade rests on. Required (minItems 1) for every grade except `no-counterpart`, where it must be empty -- enforced by the checker's cross-field rule as well as this schema's conditional, because a JSON Schema validator alone cannot be trusted to be the only enforcement point for a rule this load-bearing.

axeyum_theorem.description: A kernel declaration id, e.g. `CReal.ivt_approx`. Must resolve in the kernel projection unless `axeyum_verification` says otherwise.

mathlib_theorem.description: The comparable Mathlib lemma/instance name, or `null` if this witness is deliberately one-sided (e.g. documenting an Axeyum-only result, or a clean negative search, inside an otherwise-comparable row).

mathlib_location.description: `file:line` in the pinned mathlib4 checkout, or `null` to match `mathlib_theorem: null`.

note.description: What this specific pair shows about the grade -- e.g. "ours returns an approximate root with an explicit tolerance witness; theirs asserts existence classically".
